title: The End of the Master Builder
coreMove: Replace the master-controller reflex with distributed coordination and explicit handoffs.
sourcePressure: The source distinguishes simple, complicated, and complex problems, then uses Russia Wharf to show work too distributed for one expert to command alone.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says teamwork is good. The real chapter asks what kind of control fits work that no single mind can command.

sourceAnchors.name: Russia Wharf
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar identifies Russia Wharf as the construction example of a project too distributed for one expert to command alone.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Russia Wharf makes the old master-builder fantasy feel physically too small for the project around it.

sourceAnchors.name: simple, complicated, and complex problems
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar says the chapter uses this distinction to show that different work needs different forms of control.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A cake recipe, a rocket, and a city block do not ask for the same kind of command.

hook: No one can do it alone anymore

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: civic project leads managing engineers, tenants, and utilities
exampleSpecs.stakes: a seawall pour collides with tenant access and utility shutdowns
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Thomas replaces the single master schedule with a dependency board where each trade marks the handoff it needs from another crew
exampleSpecs.firstImage: tidewater slapping below temporary plywood stairs

exampleSpecs.domain: Maja, a university field expedition planner
exampleSpecs.audience: academic teams coordinating science, transport, permits, and safety
exampleSpecs.stakes: a remote geology trip stalls because permits, satellite phones, and sample custody are owned separately
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Maja stops asking one professor to approve everything and makes each role state its handoff trigger before departure
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "The permit is not the plan," Maja says beside a stack of sample tubes

exampleSpecs.domain: Ben, a telecom outage restoration lead
exampleSpecs.audience: technical incident leads tempted to centralize every decision
exampleSpecs.stakes: a hospital circuit remains dark while fiber, power, and access teams wait for central permission
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ben asks which decisions can be local and which must be escalated, then moves the access crew without waiting for a full-command call
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What if the bottleneck is the person trying to be helpful?

exampleSpecs.domain: Juliette, an opera stage manager in technical rehearsal
exampleSpecs.audience: creative production leads coordinating artists and safety crews
exampleSpecs.stakes: a flying set piece depends on lighting, rigging, conductor timing, and stage clearance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Juliette calls a cross-role cue pause where rigging, lights, and music each confirm the next dependency before the set piece moves
exampleSpecs.firstImage: dust drifting through a cone of blue stage light

exampleSpecs.domain: Anders, an offshore wind maintenance scheduler
exampleSpecs.audience: operations planners working around weather windows and specialist crews
exampleSpecs.stakes: a turbine repair misses its weather window if vessel, blade tech, and grid operator act from separate plans
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Anders traces the missed window to three locally correct plans that never exposed their dependencies to one another
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Anders one cancelled vessel to see that every plan had been right in isolation

exampleSpecs.domain: Lin, a public library renovation permit coordinator
exampleSpecs.audience: public-sector staff balancing contractors, public access, and inspectors
exampleSpecs.stakes: the children's wing reopens late if fire inspection and shelving installation are sequenced by one overloaded manager
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lin turns the overloaded manager's private plan into a shared handoff calendar with inspector, shelving vendor, and librarian signoffs
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You stand between bare carpet squares and boxed picture books while the inspector's voicemail plays

skillTargets: classify simple versus complicated versus complex work
identify when central control is a bottleneck

tryThisNowSpec: Take one project with more than three roles and mark the next handoff each role needs, not the task each role owns.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
